picks.intervention_label: active surveillance (guideline-aligned default; no adjuvant TKI)
picks.rationale: ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS GIST CPG 2022 and NCCN GIST v1.2026 converge on the same answer for this subtype: no adjuvant TKI, surveillance instead. ESMO 2022 states the consensus plainly, that adjuvant treatment is avoided in SDH-expression-negative GISTs, because they do not respond to imatinib and tend to run an indolent course. The natural-history data favor an imaging plan over a drug: recurrence is the rule in dSDH-GIST (~71% eventually recur or progress, median EFS ~2.5 yr post-resection), yet no adjuvant agent has been shown to bend that curve. This is the guideline default and I rank it first without hedging.
primary_concerns: SDHB IHC currently reads intact, which sits oddly against two somatic SDHA hits at ~85% combined VAF; the re-cut the profile flags has to confirm the SDH-deficient phenotype before the ESMO avoid-adjuvant consensus formally attaches to this patient.
Germline SDHA is still pending. Resolving it is itself a guideline step (NCCN GIST v1.2026 directs genetic-counseling referral for all SDH-deficient GIST), not an optional extra.

picks.intervention_label: NCI Rare Tumor Natural History Study + genetic-counseling referral (NCT03739827)
picks.rationale: NCCN GIST v1.2026 recommends genetic-counseling and germline-testing referral for every SDH-deficient GIST, and this is the route that operationalizes it. The NCI Rare Tumor Natural History Study (NCT03739827) takes SDH-deficient GIST regardless of disease status, so the NED setting is not a blocker, and it plugs the patient into the NIH Pediatric and wt-GIST referral network where the SDHA and SDHB workup actually gets settled. It satisfies the guideline and the stated trial preference at once, without committing to any unproven systemic agent.
primary_concerns: This is a natural-history and biospecimen protocol, not a therapeutic one; the value is diagnostic resolution and specialist access, not disease control.
Enrollment leans on NIH-site evaluation, which carries a travel ask on top of community-based imaging.

picks.rationale: When measurable disease returns, the guideline-endorsed first systemic move in this subtype is sunitinib, not imatinib. NCCN GIST v1.2026 carries sunitinib as a second-line option, and for SDH-deficient disease specifically the NIH cohort (Boikos 2016) reports objective response 7/38 (18%) on sunitinib versus 1/49 (2%) on imatinib, which is the published basis ESMO 2022 cites for preferring it here. The effect is modest, but it is the consensus opening move for the contingency plan.
primary_concerns: The Boikos response figures are retrospective with small per-drug n; activity in dSDH-GIST is genuine but lower than in KIT-mutant disease.
Not applicable while the patient is NED. This is a contingency anchor for first recurrence, not an action for now.

picks.rationale: NCCN GIST v1.2026 and ESMO 2022 sequence regorafenib after sunitinib, on the GRID pivotal RCT. dSDH-GIST was under-represented in GRID, so subset activity is extrapolation, characterized as modest in the von Mehren 2025 review rather than demonstrated in a dedicated dSDH cohort. It earns its place as the guideline-aligned third-line rung of the contingency ladder, with the evidence caveat stated up front.
primary_concerns: No dSDH-GIST-specific trial data; the subset claim rests on extrapolation from a KIT-mutant-dominated pivotal trial.
Contingency only, and only after sunitinib in the guideline sequence.

picks.intervention_label: clinical-trial enrollment at recurrence: SDH-deficient temozolomide cohort (NCT05661643)
picks.rationale: This is where guideline and preference line up: NCCN GIST v1.2026 explicitly prefers clinical-trial enrollment for SDH-deficient and wt-GIST, so at recurrence a trial is the endorsed path rather than a detour. The SDH-deficient temozolomide cohort (NCT05661643) is the cleanest indication match and rides single-arm phase-2 activity specific to this subtype (~40% response, Burgoyne case series). I am ranking the trial route, not temozolomide as a standard, because the drug itself is not yet guideline-endorsed.
primary_concerns: Temozolomide is off-guideline as a standard agent; the guideline-fit here is the trial-enrollment route, not the drug.
The trial requires measurable disease, so it excludes the current NED state, and NCT05661643 runs out of Asan Medical Center in Korea, a real travel constraint.
Promising newer agents in this subtype (olverembatinib, rogaratinib, belzutifan) sit in the same off-guideline trial-territory category until their readouts mature.

notes: Anchored to ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS GIST CPG 2022 and NCCN GIST v1.2026. The decisive call is that adjuvant imatinib is off-guideline for this patient: ESMO 2022 puts SDH-expression-negative GIST in the avoid-adjuvant column, and the registration RCTs (Z9001, SSGXVIII, PERSIST-5) either excluded or separated out the imatinib-insensitive genotypes this patient belongs to. If the board hears 'why not 3 years of adjuvant imatinib,' the guideline answer is that the subset was never shown to benefit and does not respond. Everything past rank 2 is contingency framing for first recurrence; nothing systemic is indicated while NED. All of it is provisional on the SDHB re-cut and germline SDHA resolution confirming the dSDH phenotype the whole plan rests on.
